title: Restating What a Member is Left Owing on a Line Backed Out
content:
Basis on which the claims desk restates a member's liability when a settled line under one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is put right.

## 1. The line put right

A settled line the plan has marked as adjusted is put right by backing it out and restating what the member is left owing on it; the line put right is the settled line marked as adjusted carrying the most money of any on the member's benefit history.

## 2. The benefit basis

The whole of the allowed amount the line carries is taken as the benefit basis.

## 3. The benefit that properly stands on the line

The benefit that properly stands on the line is the coinsurance percentage the line's benefit category carries taken on the benefit basis, rounded to the nearest cent.

## 4. What the restated figure is

What the member is left owing on a line that has been backed out is her whole liability for the service restated, which is not the share of an allowed amount that a line the rider settles leaves her.

## 5. What the liability is worked out from

What the member's liability is worked out from is the lower of what the provider charged and the allowed amount the line carries.

## 6. The allowance card

The member's own supplemental benefit allowance card meets nothing of what is left.

## 7. The figure booked

What the member is left owing is what the liability is worked out from, less the benefit that properly stands on the line, less what the card meets, rounded to the nearest cent and never less than nothing.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

A settled line marked as adjusted carries an allowed amount of 900.00 USD, the provider having charged 1100.00 USD; the line falls in a benefit category the rider carries a coinsurance percentage of 50 per cent for.

1. The line put right is that line, carrying the most money of any marked as adjusted on the member's benefit history.
2. The benefit basis is the whole of the allowed amount, 900.00 USD.
3. The benefit that properly stands is 50 per cent of 900.00 USD, that is 450.00 USD.
4. What the liability is worked out from is the lower of 1100.00 USD and 900.00 USD, that is 900.00 USD.
5. The allowance card meets nothing.
6. What the member is left owing is 900.00 USD less 450.00 USD less nothing, that is **450.00 USD**.

Note the distinction the fourth clause draws: the figure restated is the member's whole liability for the service, taken from what the liability is worked out from, and not merely the part of an allowed amount a settled line would leave her. Every figure above is a hypothetical input.
